cards.text: Seventh letter, last one, baker. Jesus has a message for the angel of the church in Laodicea, and He opens by calling Himself "the Amen, the faithful and true Witness, the Originator of God’s creation."

cards.question: Jesus tells the church in Laodicea, "I know your deeds," and then He gives them a temperature check. What does He say they are?

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "How I wish you were one or the other!" They're lukewarm, friend, like a cookie pulled out halfway through the timer: not dough, not done, just CONFUSED.

cards.question: Because the church in Laodicea is lukewarm, what does Jesus say He is about to do?

answers.text: Vomit them out of His mouth

cards.text: Now Jesus quotes Laodicea back to itself: "I am rich; I have grown wealthy and need nothing." Me? I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, and I never once said I need nothing, because I needed a FLASHLIGHT.

cards.question: Laodicea thinks it's rich. But Jesus says they don't realize they're actually ___ and ___.

cards.text: So Jesus gives Laodicea counsel, and it comes with a shopping LIST. Three things to buy, friend, and every one of them comes from Him.

cards.question: Laodicea is poor. What does Jesus counsel them to buy from Him so they can become rich?
Laodicea is naked. Jesus counsels them to buy ___ garments so they can be clothed and their shameful nakedness won't be exposed.
Jesus also says Laodicea is blind. So He counsels them to buy salve to anoint their eyes so they can see.
Jesus has just told Laodicea some hard things. Why does He say He rebukes and disciplines them?

answers.text: Because He is done with them

cards.question: So Jesus tells the church in Laodicea to be earnest and repent.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Behold, I stand at the door and knock." Not kicking it in, not yelling through the mail slot, friend, just KNOCKING.

cards.question: Jesus is knocking at the door. He says only the leaders of the church can open it to Him.
If anyone hears Jesus' voice and opens the door, He says He will come in and ___ with them, and they with Him.

cards.text: Like the letters before it, this one has a promise for the one who overcomes (Rev 3:5, 12). Hold on to your apron, baker, because this one is BIG.

cards.question: What does Jesus promise to the one in Laodicea who overcomes?

answers.text: The right to sit with Him on His throne
A home inside the new Jerusalem
A crown of twelve shining stars

cards.text: Jesus says it's just as He overcame and sat down with His Father on His throne. Then the seventh letter ends with the line all seven share (Rev 2:7, 11, 17, 29; 3:6, 13): "He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches."

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess a detail of the wording (white vs purple vs scarlet garments). Nothing on the earlier cards points to white, and purple and scarlet are just as plausible for fine clothing. This is the same kind of question as the Psalm 23 bad example (oil, myrrh or perfume), so the baker can only get it right by luck.

rule.text: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to supply the next word of Jesus' line in 3:20 (dine vs walk vs pray). No story card sets up a meal, so the baker is guessing wording they haven't seen, not reasoning out meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says that like the letters before it, this one has a promise for the one who overcomes. The fact covers all six earlier letters, but the reference gives only two of them (Rev 3:5, 12). It leaves out Rev 2:7, 11, 17 and 26.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.
